title: DHAP: Towards Efficient OLAP in a Disaggregated and Heterogeneous Environment
problem: Data systems lack adequate support for combining two key datacenter trends: hardware disaggregation and heterogeneous accelerators. Existing systems handle only homogeneous disaggregated CPUs or heterogeneous accelerators within monolithic servers.
motivation: Enable efficient OLAP query processing in disaggregated systems with heterogeneous accelerators (CPUs and GPUs) through specialized query compilation and runtime optimization.
method: The system combines a compiler and runtime. The compiler figures out the best way to execute each query across a mix of hardware types—CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs—and generates specific code for each. The runtime then executes these queries using pipelined stages (running different parts in parallel) while minimizing data movement between machines and ensuring no machine runs out of memory.
key_novelty: This is the first system to handle analytics workloads across disaggregated resources (computing machines spread across a network) paired with diverse hardware accelerators (different types like GPUs and FPGAs).
contributions: Query compiler with planning module for heterogeneous disaggregated systems
Runtime system for pipelined OLAP execution on disaggregated CPU/GPU nodes
Near-optimal solutions with significant latency improvements
limitations: No specific numbers for individual optimization components; unclear how much benefit comes from compiler vs runtime.
primary_theme: Query Processing in Disaggregated Heterogeneous Datacenters
